principles: A PEMS badge X authorises X and above; the columns in pems_table.json encode that spread.

An inline level token inside PEMS row text (e.g. '(I / P)', '[EMR]', 'I/P only:') governs the clause it sits in, not the whole row. A row with two clause-scoped levels is compound; the site may split it and no badge override is written.
A bracketed badge ([A], [I]) is that level plus a special requirement; the site must reproduce the bracket, not drop it.
A site row that elaborates an intervention with no PEMS row of its own inherits the level of the intervention's row; it is an authoring question, not a badge fix.

No badge override was written: neither contradictory badge (p.61#4 EMT, p.63#7 I) is wrong. The constraints on those rows are clause-scoped inline tokens, so overriding the badge would corrupt the source record. The resolutions live here, on the site cells.
